entries.quote: HER2 L869R is a neratinib-sensitive, gain-of-function mutation
entries.cited_text: Laboratory studies suggested that HER2 L869R is a neratinib-sensitive, gain-of-function mutation that upon dimerization with mutant HER3 E928G , also present in the breast cancer, amplifies HER2 signaling.

entries.quote: acquired HER2 T798I gatekeeper mutation ... with acquired resistance to neratinib
entries.cited_text: We report a HER2 T798I gatekeeper mutation in a patient with HER2 L869R -mutant breast cancer with acquired resistance to neratinib. Upon clinical progression, HER2 T798I was detected in plasma tumor cell-free DNA. Neratinib blocked HER2-mediated signaling and growth in cells expressing HER2 L869R but not HER2 L869R/T798I In contrast, afatinib and the osimertinib metabolite AZ5104 strongly suppressed HER2 L869R/T798I -induced signaling and cell growth.

entries.quote: afatinib strongly suppressed HER2 L869R/T798I -induced signaling and cell growth
entries.cited_text: Neratinib blocked HER2-mediated signaling and growth in cells expressing HER2 L869R but not HER2 L869R/T798I In contrast, afatinib and the osimertinib metabolite AZ5104 strongly suppressed HER2 L869R/T798I -induced signaling and cell growth. Treatment with afatinib and AZ5104 blocked phosphorylation of HER2WT as well as both HER2 mutants. Both neratinib and osimertinib failed to suppress growth of MCF10A/HER2L869R/T798I cells in 3D Matrigel, whereas this was completely blocked by afatinib and AZ5104, suggesting that the latter two inhibitors are able to overcome HER2T798I-mediated drug resistance. While afatinib and neratinib are both irreversible covalent EGFR/HER2 TKIs, we found that afatinib, but not neratinib, was able to block HER2L869R/T798I activity. Treatment with low doses of afatinib (10 nM), easily achievable in patients (), completely blocked growth of MCF10A/HER2L869R/T798I cells, while treatment with neratinib at clinically achievable concentrations () failed to do so (Fig. 4A,B).
